reasoning_traces.think:
The maturity model establishes a hierarchical lattice of component readiness, where each level imposes stricter constraints on design token usage, accessibility, and governance. At Level 0, components are drafts without compliance; at Level 1, they must pass design token audits. As levels increase, more stringent checks—like accessibility validation, claim governance, and performance profiling—are enforced. This progression enables a probabilistic inference engine (GSI) to estimate component readiness based on observable compliance metrics. The GSE leverages these levels as state machines, transitioning components through defined gates to ensure only production-ready artifacts are promoted. Failure modes include bypassing design tokens, introducing accessibility regressions, or violating claim governance, which trigger demotion or rejection.
